description: A MARK THAT KNOWS WHAT IT POINTS AT. Name the element — a CSS selector — and the box is looked up from the page itself at capture time, so the same instruction draws the correct picture today, after a fix, and at another screen width. An arrow drawn on an ordinary screenshot points at a coordinate: right when it was drawn, wrong the moment anything re-renders. That is why annotated screenshots are disposable, and it is the whole difference here. It is also how a picture marks ITSELF: a finding already carries a selector, so «draw the contrast failures» needs no aiming — pass their selectors straight through. Shapes: `box` (outline it), `pin` (a numbered dot at its corner — for ordered things like a tab route), `arrow` and `line` (from one element to another, which is how you show an error message wired to the wrong field), and `blur` (a pane that makes the element unreadable — an address, a customer's name, a token in a staging header). Colours are named, not free: default · bad · good · info · warn. A LABEL IS A CALLOUT, not a sticker: it is placed in free space beside its element, clear of every other mark, and joined to the outline by a leader line ending in a dot. So «outline the payment block and say what is wrong with it» comes back as one readable statement instead of words stamped over the thing they are about. A mark whose element is not on the page is REPORTED in `missed`, never silently dropped — a reader who sees three arrows must be able to trust that there were three things to point at. Read-only: it photographs and draws, and touches nothing — a blur hides the data in THIS picture, never on the page, so the next capture shows it again.

fromFindings.description: Instead of naming marks yourself, DRAW THE PAGE'S OWN FINDINGS: every finding that carries a selector becomes an outlined box with its title beside it, coloured by severity. A finding already knows where it is, so nobody has to aim — this is the picture a tester currently makes by hand, one arrow at a time. Combine with `marks` to add your own.

marks.description: Up to 60 marks. More than that covers the picture instead of marking it.

box.description: Or a box in IMAGE pixels, if you already have one from a shot map

label.description: Short text on the mark — three characters inside a pin, up to sixty in a callout placed beside the element and joined to it by a leader line

pad.description: For 'blur': extra margin round the element, in CSS pixels (default 2) — a pane flush with the text tends to leave the tops of the letters showing

toSelector.description: For arrow/line: the element at the other end

path.description: Write the marked PNG here instead of returning it inline

tabId.description: Target tab (from qa_tabs); omit for the active tab
